title: GOVERN: Establish AI governance and accountability
text: Set governance structures, policies, and accountable owners for AI risk management. Define approval gates, change control, monitoring responsibilities, and escalation authorities. Governance should produce traceable decisions: what was approved, by whom, based on which evidence.

title: MAP: Intended use, context, and stakeholders
text: Map intended purpose, users, affected stakeholders, and deployment context. Identify foreseeable misuse and harms, including security abuse and privacy leakage. Good mapping turns vague risks into explicit scenarios with signals and mitigations.

title: MEASURE: Risk measurement and evaluation
text: Measure trustworthiness characteristics and risk indicators aligned to use context (reliability, robustness, fairness, privacy, security). Define metrics, test plans, and acceptance thresholds. Measurement artifacts are evidence for governance decisions and post-deployment monitoring baselines.

title: MANAGE: Risk response and mitigation loop
text: Prioritize mitigations, implement controls, and track residual risks over time. Define what triggers re-evaluation (incidents, drift, major updates, new threats). Risk management is a loop: measure → act → verify → learn.

title: Document policies and procedures as operational controls
text: Maintain written policies for AI development/use, approvals, change control, monitoring, and incident response. Tie policy requirements to concrete artifacts (checklists, logs, dashboards, runbooks). The key is enforceability and repeatability, not aspirational statements.

title: Stakeholder impact identification and engagement
text: Identify who may be impacted and what harms could occur, including vulnerable groups. Incorporate stakeholder needs into requirements, testing, and governance review. Document decisions and unresolved concerns to preserve transparency and accountability.

title: Risk register and decision traceability
text: Track risks, mitigations, owners, evidence links, and review cadence in a maintained risk register. Each risk should connect to tests, incidents, and changes. A risk register is the organization’s memory: it enables explainability under pressure.

title: Continuous monitoring and improvement
text: Monitor deployed systems for drift, misuse, emergent harms, and performance regressions. Define alerts and response actions (rollback/fallback, escalation, patching). Feed monitoring results back into evaluation plans and risk register updates.

title: Test failure modes and adversarial behavior
text: Test for failure modes and unsafe behaviors under realistic and adversarial conditions. For LLMs, include prompt injection, data leakage attempts, and hallucination stress tests. Keep test reports as evidence for controls and residual risk decisions.

title: Security within AI risk management
text: Address cybersecurity risks for AI components, data pipelines, interfaces, and operational workflows. Use threat modeling and map threats to mitigations (access control, rate limiting, monitoring). Security is part of explainability: you can explain how you prevented misuse and how you would respond.
